issues: Covers rose week on week on a busier weekend with students returning and a home match, and were roughly flat year on year.
Spend per head was flat week on week and down year on year, with discounts weighing on it.
Sales rose sharply week on week and finished above target but remain down year on year.
Labour was held tightly, with the much higher sales taken for almost no extra labour spend, although the budget rota overspent because of two freshers fairs.
Food usage variance ran above plan and drinks below; more tonkotsu broth use, the student ramen vouchers and app discounts are expected to push food cost up further.
A few undercooked pink chicken karaage pieces were found, so the team is probing every batch from the fryer and cooking smaller batches.
Deliveroo late prepared orders are higher than wanted but acceptable, prep time is strong, and inaccurate orders are again higher than wanted.
Four Deliveroo refund claims were received and all were disputed.
Google reviews were mostly five star, with a single two star review.
The air conditioning is an ultra high priority maintenance job with Ross, and the front door service and accessible lift check are medium priority.
The extraction units are being checked on the close on 01/10/2026.
Two team members were off during the week; shifts were covered with support from the M15 team.
A new team incentive game is being built and should go live next week.
Pest control, fire safety, electrical, gas and ventilation compliance were all completed.
Freshers fair, the student ramen offer, the lunch menu, XOXO and a student lock in from 15:00 to 20:00 on Monday 28/09/2026 are the live and upcoming promotions.
Sales, labour and cleanliness are the areas for improvement, and no staffing changes or recruitment are needed.
EDI/NEW 22/09: Sales hit target for the first time in seven weeks.
EDI/NEW 22/09: The air conditioning units are 21 years old and inaccessible, maintenance has recommended replacing them and Ross Ward has been notified.
EDI/NEW 22/09: The new incentive game will focus on spend per head and reviews.
